topic: What happens if you stare at the sun?
title: What Happens If You Stare At The Sun?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Photic retinopathy' (accessed 2026-11-17): damage to the eye's retina, particularly the macula, from prolonged exposure to solar radiation; includes solar retinopathy

Wikipedia, 'Photic retinopathy' (accessed 2026-11-17): retinal damage appears to occur primarily due to photochemical injury rather than thermal injury; the temperature rise from looking at the Sun with a 3-mm pupil only causes a 4 degree C increase, insufficient to photocoagulate; light promotes oxidation - chemical reactions occur in exposed tissues with unbonded oxygen molecules

Wikipedia, 'Photic retinopathy' (accessed 2026-11-17): symptoms include a spot in vision that does not go away, blurring, eye pain or headaches; impairment usually in both eyes; 20/20 vision usually ends up about 20/40 or 20/60, but can be far worse; mild cases show a foveal yellow spot in the first days, replaced by a reddish dot often surrounded by pigment after a few days

Wikipedia, 'Photic retinopathy' (accessed 2026-11-17): generally goes away on its own over time but there is no specific treatment known to be reliable for speeding recovery; people generally recover visual acuity completely within two months, though severe cases may take longer or never see complete recovery

American Academy of Ophthalmology, 'How to Watch a Solar Eclipse Safely' (patient guidance, accessed 2026-11-17): never look directly at the sun without certified solar filters (ISO 12312-2 eclipse glasses); ordinary sunglasses are not safe; documented surge of solar retinopathy cases after the 2017 eclipse (JAMA Ophthalmology studies of eclipse-related macular injury)

lines.text: What happens if you stare at the sun?
Your lens focuses sunlight onto your retina.
Like a magnifying glass on a leaf.
But here is the twist: it is not a burn.
lines.caps: HERE IS THE *TWIST | IT IS | *NOT A BURN

lines.text: Your retina warms about four degrees.
That leaves a yellow spot on your macula.
Doctors see it turn red within days.
You get a blind spot that will not go away.
lines.caps: YOU GET A *BLIND SPOT | THAT WILL | *NOT GO AWAY

lines.text: Vision drops to about 20/40, sometimes far worse.
Usually in both eyes at once.
It usually heals within a month or two.
lines.caps: IT *USUALLY HEALS | WITHIN A | *MONTH OR TWO

lines.text: But severe cases never fully recover.
After every eclipse, eye clinics see the damage.
So never look directly. Use eclipse glasses.
